decisions.reason: As a close extension of the established offer that already has its own webpage, Product A likely meets at least provisional aspirations in an expanding firm with enough slack to continue supporting it.

Because Product B builds directly on the firm's automation offer and the firm is growing with active R&D, management is more likely to keep it despite somewhat higher uncertainty signaled by only a website mention.

Product C is close to the core formwork business, so in a growing medium-sized German machinery firm it would usually be retained unless clearly underperforming, though its limited web prominence raises the chance of later pruning.
Product D fits the firm's modular formwork portfolio and its own dedicated webpage suggests stronger commitment and acceptable early results, making withdrawal unlikely in the next year.
Given its close fit with the established product system and dedicated web presentation, Product E is likely to be kept while the firm continues planned growth and exploitation of related innovations.

Although Product F is only mentioned on the website and may face overlap with related magnetic components, the firm's expansion, technical capabilities, and portfolio logic still make retention more likely than withdrawal.
